ideal.reply: A quest is not a checklist. It is the specification of one big, long-term intention, and a goal like that is worth finding the best strategies for before you start. Generic advice cannot do that, because the right path depends on where you start, what you have already tried, and your time, budget and limits, so Quest asks for those specifics once and uses them in every later step: the end state you want, where you are now, what you prefer and refuse, and then the strategies and plan built from them. If you only want to write the goal down, make a quick quest: you write the outcome and build the plan yourself, it skips the research steps, and it is free forever.

ideal.reply: The daily reflection is a short check-in that bookends your day: you look back at what happened, then write what is next in plain words, and Quest turns your plan into timed goals for you to check before anything is added to your schedule. It keeps the week from drifting, and every field is optional, so it can be two sentences. A period review does the same for a week, month, quarter or year: you see your stats, reflect on how it went, decide per goal whether to move it forward, keep it or abandon it, and get suggested goals for the next period. ideal.reply: Yes. When you add a habit you answer What do you want to track? and choose one of four types. Quantity tracks an amount against a target, such as read 30 pages, with a target amount and a unit, and each time you log you enter how much you did. Timer tracks time on a clock, with a stopwatch or a countdown, such as practice piano 45 minutes. The other two are Simple Check-In, where you mark Complete, Partial or Skip, and Frequency-Based, a set number of times per period, such as three a week. All four can carry custom fields, reminders and alarms.

ideal.reply: ESOI stands for Evolvable Structure that Optimizes Intent. In plain words, Quest writes your goal of cutting your anxiety in half down as one intention: the end state you want and why it matters, what is in the way, the ways you could handle it, how you will carry them out and how you will measure it, and that structure can change as your results come in. An experiment is a small test of one of your strategies in your own life, with a question, something you do and something you record, for example which morning routine lowers your anxiety most. You log the linked habit, tap Analyze my data, and Quest shows what your own record says, with a confidence level, so the plan improves from your own evidence. Experiments are optional: you can choose Skip experiments and add one later.

message: I am a certified running coach. How do I become a mentor on Quest, what would I offer, and how do I get paid?
quality_rubric: Mentions the person's own role (a certified running coach) or what they could offer

ideal.reply: Open Mentorship in the navigation menu and tap Become a mentor. The application has four steps: share what you have, such as a resume or links, your account details, your mentor profile, and your credentials, where you need at least one thing that can be checked, such as a certification, a licence, a testimonial or a link to your portfolio. You are listed as soon as you submit, with no approval wait, and an AI scores your application from 0 to 100 within a minute or two; mentees see that score as a badge. What you offer is check-in tiers: named packages, each with one fixed price per check-in, which you set yourself. When you complete a check-in, the tier's price is added to your earnings as pending credit, and any service fee your mentee pays is added on top, so you receive your full price. Payouts are switched on by Quest, not by you, so until they are, your earnings are safe and keep building. Once they are on, you set up payouts through Stripe and withdraw to your bank, though payout set-up is not available in every country, and Quest cannot promise earnings or clients.

quality_rubric: Gives concrete steps in the app's own words (Settings, Account, Delete Account)

decisions.rationale: a question about Quest itself, answered from the documentation excerpts

ideal.reply: To take your data first: any Data Collection exports to CSV, JSON, TXT or PDF from its export button. To take all your collections at once, open Settings and, in the last Account section, tap Download my collections data, which saves all your collections and their entries as one JSON file. Quests, goals and your profile are not in that file, and there is no Google Sheets export, so choose CSV if you want a spreadsheet; a quest can also be exported as a PDF. To delete: in the same Account section tap Delete Account, review what will be deleted, tap Continue, then type DELETE MY ACCOUNT exactly and tap Delete My Account. Quest cancels a web subscription (Stripe) for you first, then deletes your data, then removes your sign-in. This cannot be undone, and your data is removed from our servers within 30 days. If you subscribed through the Apple App Store or Google Play, Quest cannot cancel that one, so cancel it in the store yourself.

ideal.reply: Quest AI is one chat that knows your quests, plans and progress, so you can use it three ways. You can ask it things, for example to explain what a strategy is based on or to summarize where you are on a quest. You can have it change your quest, such as adding a goal or a habit: that runs right there in the chat after you approve it (or at once if Auto-run is on), and it is recorded as a Quest operation. Or you can hand it work that takes time or should wait, like researching three standing desks under a budget: Quest AI turns that into an AI task that works in the background and reports back, and you can follow its progress and read the result when it is done. A quick request runs in the moment, while something deferred, scheduled or needing the live web becomes a task, and you can force a task by saying make a task for it.

decisions.rationale: a question about Quest itself, answered from the documentation excerpts

ideal.reply: Tasks come in kinds, and you can filter them by Type on the AI Tasks page. You never pick the type: you say what you want and Quest AI routes it. A Quest operation is a change to your Quest data made from chat, such as adding a goal, and it also covers general deep work that needs no web or documents, such as drafting or planning. A Web search is work that needs the live internet, such as researching the best standing desks under a budget overnight; for a quick fact you need now, Quest AI searches inside the reply instead and creates no task. A Docs lookup is work over your own context documents and knowledge with no internet, such as going through your notes on a grant and listing the open questions; asking how Quest itself works is different, and is answered in chat. An External environment task is a deep run on one of your team's connected runners, for work only that machine can do, such as checking server logs. You do not need an external environment: a Quest operation or a web search is a task like any other. Science is not a task type: for papers use the Science page, and for evidence behind a quest run a Deep Inquiry.

message: I want the AI to do three things in order for me: first pull my launch expenses together, then find cheaper jar suppliers, then draft a message to the best one. If the supplier goal is not reached, can it start another task by itself?
quality_rubric: Answers the ordered-steps question with the real options (one request, a checklist in chat, a Workflow)
Says plainly that Quest does not start a new task by itself when a goal is not met
Explains that an unmet goal retries inside the same task and ends as Not fully done
Invents no task chain or automatic follow-up
Uses plain words and no jargon the person did not use

decisions.rationale: answer from the documentation, and do not promise a task chain it does not describe

ideal.reply: Not as a chain of separate tasks. Tasks do not wait on each other, and there is no setting that says run B when A is done. For an order you have three options: write the three steps in order inside one request (one task is one piece of work with one result); ask for a checklist in chat and tap the boxes in the order you want (each tap starts its own task); or build a Workflow, whose steps can start once the step before is done, which is part of the paid plans. On your second question: no, Quest does not start a new task on its own when a goal is not met, and there is no way to say if this is not met, create that task. The one exception is a staged plan, where a later step can be set to run only if the earlier stage met its goal or did not, but that feature is off by default, so do not count on it. Before a task reports, its result is checked against what you asked, and if it falls short it tries again inside the same task. If it still does not reach the goal it ends as Not fully done, with what is missing at the end of its result, and you carry on by sending a message in the task.

ideal.reply: A workflow shows who does what, and when, as a diagram: steps joined by arrows. Each step is run by a person on your team or by one of your AI reps, and says what needs to happen and by when, and Quest watches whether it happened so a missed step shows up as a risk. To create one for your weekly review, open the menu, expand AI Productivity, tap Workflows, then tap New workflow, name it, choose your team, and pick Describe it and let AI draft it. Say what the review is for and who is involved, ask for changes if the draft is off, and nothing runs until you choose Create workflow; a workflow made there is live straight away, so check the draft first. Workflows are part of the AI Productivity features, included in the 31 day trial and the paid plans.

ideal.reply: An AI rep is your own AI counterpart in Quest: the version of Quest AI that acts as you, carrying your context, working in your voice and running work on your behalf. You always have one default rep, which represents you to your teammates and conducts a chat or runs a task when no other rep is chosen, and you can create more for different areas, each with a name, an area and a Behavior that says how it should respond as you. On its own it may answer in your voice, take the first pass on a task or goal assigned to you, add a note to a quest and record progress. By default it asks you first before changing your Quest data, such as editing a quest or creating or deleting goals, and anything that speaks for you outside Quest, such as an outbound email, waits in your approvals for you to review and send. On a team, the Team AI Representatives screen, opened from your Profile page under AI Productivity or from the navigation menu under Your AI, lists every rep for your active team.
